speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you've brought in your infant for bilious vomiting and an inability to pass meconium. To understand the severity, has the baby been passing any gas, and when was the last time they had a bowel movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (Congenital Aganglionic Megacolon).

The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and the failure to pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life is highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. To confirm this, I am requesting an Anorectal Manometry and an Abdominal X-Ray.
